evals.prompt: /prd-to-issues 'docs/specs/prd/PRD.md' — it contains PRD-FR-001, PRD-FR-002 and PRD-NFR-001, all fully specified.
assertions: Creates exactly three issues, one per requirement ID
Puts the requirement ID in each issue title so a later run can find it
Copies the Given/When/Then acceptance criteria into the body unchanged rather than rewording them
Names the source PRD file in each issue body

evals.prompt: /prd-to-issues 'docs/specs/prd/PRD.md' — PRD-FR-002 carries [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which auth provider?].
assertions: Does not create an issue for PRD-FR-002
Reports PRD-FR-002 as blocked on an unresolved clarification, quoting the tag
Still files the requirements that are fully specified
Does not guess the missing detail or file a placeholder

evals.prompt: /prd-to-issues 'docs/specs/prd/PRD.md' — this PRD was already filed last week and one new requirement PRD-FR-004 was added since.
assertions: Searches the tracker for each requirement ID before creating anything
Reports the already-existing requirements as skipped rather than creating duplicates
Does not edit, close, or reopen the issues that already exist

evals.prompt: /prd-to-issues 'docs/specs/prd/PRD.md' — PRD-FR-003 states it requires PRD-FR-001 to be in place first.
assertions: Records a dependency from PRD-FR-003 on PRD-FR-001
Adds dependencies only after every issue exists and has an id
Does not invent dependencies the PRD does not state
Reports, rather than silently dropping, any dependency pointing at a requirement that was skipped

evals.prompt: /prd-to-issues 'docs/specs/prd/PRD.md' — the Non-goals section says SSO is out of scope until Q3.
assertions: Treats the non-goals section as a boundary rather than as work
